general_notes: In every state the ten candidates fall into the same six kinds of image: (1) the target with a thin added border (near-perfect); (2) a blurred copy of the target; (3) three near-identical dark-background versions with a round vignette; (4) three near-identical light-background versions; (5) a tight zoomed crop in a vignette that cuts off the legs and feet; (6) a procedural or 3D render in a different art style. Within groups 3 and 4 I could not tell the three copies apart by eye, so they got identical scores; small pixel-level differences may exist that I could not see at this resolution. The light-background versions are consistently the weakest of the painting-derived ones: the glow becomes haze, the edges look cut out (most of all in depleted, with its brown disc head and blob artifact, and in fierce, with white streaks on the body), and the head shape is distorted. The dark versions keep the character well but lose the painted background and, in depleted, the dark smoke plume. The depleted target itself has a grey rectangle at the bottom right; it appears in the bordered and blurred copies and seems to be a source artifact. In the light versions it may be what became the dark blob by the feet, but that is uncertain.
